sections.h2: Where is Terrell County, and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Terrell County is in southwest Georgia, with Dawson as both the county seat and the only city. Wikipedia's county entry gives it 338 square miles, 335 of them land, and says it was founded on February 16, 1856 and named for William Terrell. Bronwood, Parrott and Sasser are the three towns.

Most of the county, the western and southern two thirds, drains to Ichawaynochaway Creek in the Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint basin, and the northeastern third drains to the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee sub-basin. U.S. 82 is the main east-west road, joined by State Routes 32, 41, 45, 49, 50, 55, 118 and 520. Webster, Sumter, Lee, Dougherty, Calhoun and Randolph counties are the neighbors.

Terrell County is losing people. The Census Bureau counted 9,185 in 2020 and estimates 8,656 for July 2025, a 5.7% drop from its 2020 base. A seller here is working in a shrinking market of about 27 residents per square mile, where a parcel outside Dawson may be a farmhouse with acreage and a parcel inside it a small house on a city lot.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Terrell County homes and incomes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Terrell County was valued at $118,400 for 2020-2024, and 61.6% of housing units are lived in by their owners. The figures below come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page.

Five building permits and 92.8% of residents staying put point to a stable, older housing stock. Roughly one resident in four is 65 or older, so estates and inherited houses make up a visible share of what changes hands. The profile also lists 3,383 households at 2.53 people each and a 22.6 minute average commute.

sections.h2: Which Terrell County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's main office is at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 484, Dawson, GA 39842. The county's tax website lists the phone as (229) 995-5151 and hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

  • Tax commissioner, (229) 995-5151: bills, payments, penalties and levies.
  • Tax assessor, (229) 995-5210, P.O. Box 382: values, returns, homestead applications and mobile home registration.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse deed room: copies of a warranty deed.
  • Board of Commissioners, (229) 995-4476: curbside trash for homes outside the four cities.

First-time homeowners are asked to bring a copy of their warranty deed when they file for homestead, so a recent buyer should collect it from the deed room before visiting the assessors.

sections.h2: When are Terrell County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The county's pages give two answers, so use the date on your bill. The general information page says property taxes are due by December 20 each year, while the FAQ says that beginning in 2018, real estate and business personal property taxes are due November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1 on both pages.

The general information page spells out the late steps for real estate:

  • Interest is added on the 2nd of each month at prime plus 3% divided by 12.
  • A FIFA lien is filed with the Clerk of Courts 30 days from the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5% penalty is added after 120 days, and again every 120 days, to a maximum of 20%.
  • An account that stays unpaid goes to a collection firm, and administrative and levy fees of up to $240.00 plus are added.

Those fees cover certified notices and a title search to prepare the property for sale, and the property is advertised for four weeks in the Herald Journal before a sale. The office accepts a United States Postal Service postmark on mailed payments, and a metered mark does not count.

sections.h2: What is different about Terrell County mobile home taxes?
sections.html:
Mobile and modular homes are taxed as personal property. The owner of a mobile home in the county on January 1 pays the tax by April 1 and gets a location permit at that time, and bills are usually mailed on January 2.

Missing the date triggers a 10% penalty, and the county may issue a citation for Magistrate Court or even sell the home. Past due mobile home accounts collect interest on the 16th of each month, a 10% penalty goes on April 2, and a FIFA is filed 30 days after the delinquent notice. The decal must be on display, and the assessors can be reached at (229) 995-5210.

If the home was bought or sold this year, confirm which owner paid the permit tax before closing.

sections.h2: How do homestead, special programs and appeals work in Terrell County?
sections.html:
Homestead applications are filed with the Board of Tax Assessors, and the county's FAQ says you must both own and occupy the home as of January 1. The application can be filed at any point in the year but must arrive by April 1 of the tax year to count, or the exemption starts the next year. Once approved, it stays in place until you move.

The tax website says Terrell County has local exemptions, and that a local amount replaces the state amount when it is larger. Ask the assessors for the current numbers. Owners 62 and older may qualify for more, and a deferral program lets owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less defer tax until ownership changes or the deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value.

Farmland programs assess agricultural property at 30 percent instead of 40, and Conservation Use values land by its current use. Each requires a covenant to keep the use for at least ten years.

An owner who disagrees with a value has 45 days from the notice date to appeal, and the grounds are taxability, value or uniformity. If the assessors do not agree, the appeal goes to the Board of Equalization, with arbitration as an alternative and Superior Court after that. If an owner is away on armed forces duty, a friend or family member may file within 90 days of the notice.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Terrell County house with taxes due?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner at (229) 995-5151 and request a written balance for each year, plus any mobile home account. Ask whether a FIFA has been filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, because the lien must be cleared when the deed is recorded.

Georgia property is valued as of January 1 each year, so the commissioner's office can explain how it will bill the year of your sale. Tell the title company about every open balance early, since a lien discovered at the closing table pushes the date back. Properties that have gone to the collection stage cost more to clear, because the administrative and levy fees described above are added to the balance.

An all-cash buyer who takes a house in its current condition can pay taxes from your proceeds and close without repairs or a long listing period.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Terrell County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: The number is (229) 995-5151. The office is at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 484.

faqs.q: When are Terrell County property taxes due, November 15 or December 20?
faqs.a: The county's own pages disagree. The general information page says December 20 and the FAQ says November 15, beginning in 2018. Follow the date printed on your bill, and call the office if it is unclear.

faqs.q: When is the Terrell County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want the exemption. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and bring your warranty deed if you are a first-time homeowner.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Terrell County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the notice, and the grounds are taxability, value or uniformity. A complaint about the tax amount is not a basis for appeal.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Terrell County taxes?
faqs.a: Interest starts the 2nd of the month after the due date, a FIFA lien is filed after 30 days from the delinquent notice, and a 5% penalty builds every 120 days up to 20%. A long unpaid account goes to a collection firm and can end in a sale.
